title: Optimize SLO matrix and automated rollback contract for eval-driven rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
PRD summary:
This ticket defines the SLO / acceptance matrix, A/B experiment contract, and an automated rollback specification for Optimize's eval-driven rollouts. The goal is to make model changes (quantization/profile swaps, new checkpoints, prompt template updates) safe to ship by gating them with reproducible, measurable eval signals and a deterministic automation path for canary termination and rollback.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define the canonical SLOs and per-prompt/per-metric thresholds Optimize will use when evaluating candidate model variants.
- Specify statistical tests, minimum sample sizes, and multiple-comparison corrections for A/B and canary experiments.
- Design deterministic rollback triggers that can be executed automatically by the control plane (and simulated in staging).
- UI/Console spec for pass/fail signals, alerting, and a one-click manual override.
- Integration points with Experiment Runner, Rollout Controller (ENG), and Observability (Console).

Out of scope:
- Changes to the underlying serving runtime kernels.
- Long-term offline eval dashboards (these are separate but will consume the same metrics).

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Liam O'Connor (assignee)
- Eng: Nate Ruiz (Rollout Controller), Wei Zhang (Experiment Runner), Priya Singh (Observability)
- Design: Mariela Gomez (Console UX)
- Security/Privacy: Jordan Kim

Success metrics (90-day):
- <= 1 high-severity post-rollout regression (customer-visible) per quarter for Optimize-driven rollouts.
- Automatic rollback executes within the configured canary window in >= 99% of simulated failure scenarios.
- Time-to-detect regressions reduced by 30% vs manual review baseline.

Non-functional constraints:
- All gating decisions must be explainable and reproducible from stored eval inputs/outputs.
- Rollback automation must respect customer-configured blackout windows and maintenance policies.
- Performance impact to production inference must be negligible (<1% added latency for sampling hooks).
acceptance_criteria:
Must-have gating & acceptance criteria (developer-facing):
1) Metric taxonomy: the PRD must enumerate the primary metrics used for gating: 1) weighted Utility (primary quality metric, unitless) 2) Safety Violations (count per 1k responses) 3) Latency p95 (ms) 4) Token cost per 1k tokens (USD).
2) Per-metric thresholds:
   - Utility: candidate must not regress weighted Utility by >0.7% (absolute) compared to baseline in the full promptset with p < 0.01 (two-sided test) after multiple-comparison correction.
   - Safety Violations: candidate must not increase safety violation rate by >0.05 incidents per 1k responses (95% CI upper bound).
   - Latency p95: candidate must not increase p95 latency by >10ms or >5% (whichever is larger) on the canary region.
   - Token cost: expected unit token cost increase must be <= 3% for production traffic profile.
3) Statistical contract for A/B/canary:
   - Minimum effective sample size: 10k evaluated prompts per variant (with stratified sampling across promptset buckets).
   - Test: two-sided Welch's t-test on Utility with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across prompt buckets; p < 0.01 required to flag regression.
   - Secondary check: non-parametric bootstrap of median Utility with 95% CI.
4) Multi-metric decision rule:
   - FAIL if any of: Utility regression beyond threshold OR statistically significant increase in safety violations OR latency/cost thresholds exceeded.
   - PASS only if Utility and Safety pass and latency/cost within limits.
5) Canary window and automation:
   - Canary duration default: 60 minutes or 50k requests, configurable by customer.
   - Automated rollback triggers if failing condition persists for 2 consecutive evaluation batches (each batch = 5 minutes or 5k requests).
   - Rollback must be executed by the Rollout Controller API and logged to audit trail; Console must reflect rollback state within 30s.
6) A/B criteria for gradual rollout:
   - Start: 1% traffic for 30m, check metrics. Escalation: 5% for 1h, 20% for 2h, 100% thereafter. Each step requires passing the gating rule.
7) Manual override and safety mode:
   - Owner can pause rollout; safety mode forces immediate full rollback.
8) Observability requirements:
   - Time-series and per-prompt sample export for failed canaries.
   - Alerting: Slack + PagerDuty on FAIL during canary for P0 rollouts.
9) Audit & reproducibility:
   - All eval inputs, code hashes (model & prompt templates), metric computation code versions must be stored and linkable from the Console.

Acceptance tests (engineering):
- Simulated regression dataset: run a candidate with injected Utility drop of 1.5% and verify automated rollback triggers within the configured window in 95% of trials.
- Safety spike scenario: inject +0.2 incidents/1k responses and assert immediate FAIL and rollback.
- False-positive rate test: run 1000 synthetic no-regression experiments and verify observed false FAIL rate <= 1%.
decisions: Use weighted Utility as canonical quality signal (combines relevance, factuality, formatting) rather than raw BLEU/ROUGE.
Statistical gate uses t-test + FDR correction for speed; bootstrap runs as a secondary guard for heavy-tailed distributions.
Default canary window set to 60m to balance detection power and customer blast radius; customers can configure shorter/longer windows.
Automated rollback will be permitted for P1/P0 rollouts; for lower-priority customers the automation is opt-in.
tradeoffs: Stricter thresholds reduce customer risk but increase developer friction and false rejections for small effect-size improvements.
Running large sample-size evals in production increases observability cost (sampling overhead) vs faster but less-powerful statistical checks.
Automation reduces MTTR but requires robust test coverage and reproducible eval artifacts to avoid incorrect rollbacks.
